analysis:
Examined both inference documentation excerpts, file metadata, the native-library revision change and all event-bridge patch hunks against the canonical index and supplied T-041 details. EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift head lines 15, 32 and 64 introduce and forward an optional request-owned stopStringScope; lines 159–160 pass it into matched-stop reporting on stop/length completion. This visibly changes usage attribution, not response encryption, authorization or reservation release. No concrete regression is established by these hunks.

The documentation change at docs/architecture/inference.md:2126 describes excluding reasoning/tool spans for Gemma 4 and think parsers, retaining Harmony final-message scoping and leaving diffusion output unscoped. The supplied surrounding lines 4923–5433 describe sealed cluster transport, tenant-partitioned prefixes, media lifetime fences, qualification restrictions and bilateral retirement; the complete range map identifies these as unchanged context, not newly introduced attack surface.

Material integration limit: libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 advances the native inference dependency, but its implementation diff is absent. Review that diff together with CBv2StopStringScope/ReasoningStopScope, EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift and submission callers to verify initial reasoning state, malformed/fragmented tool delimiters, scope propagation and parity between actual stopping and reported matched sequences. Check whether reporting affects billing (A-009), and ensure hidden output and stop behavior preserve A-001/TB-007 contracts. Native changes also require checking cancellation (T-010), memory ownership (T-028), and cache scoping/staging (T-041); the revision pointer alone cannot establish their preservation. No finding is inferred from missing implementation evidence.
